thread:
Jenny (AE): Orchid Labs renewal - they want to move from Committed-12 (2x GPUs) down to a hybrid consumption model. Asking for a one-time 30% concession to cover integration delays + an "ingress fee" waiver. Need guidance on pricing and whether we can allow a consumption overlay.
Priya (AM): Do they want to shorten the term or keep 12 months? Any security or compliance asks outstanding?
Jenny (AE): They want to keep 12 months but split into Reserved baseline + pay-as-you-go burst. Security Qs: SCIM SSO cert, SOC2 attestation copy requested, and they want logs retained 24 months (we default 12).
Nate (SE): For the hybrid model: technically fine, we can expose a burst pool. We'll need to pin baseline capacity to avoid cold-starts. Also FYI their POC used quantized models with longer tail latency - I can recommend a smaller baseline.
Lena (DealDesk): 30% one-time concession is outside policy. Standard renewal concessions cap at 12% for SMB deals; above that requires CRO approval + Finance sign-off. Ingress fee waivers are negotiable for strategic deals but need a clear offset (e.g., extended term or add-on commitment).
Tom (Finance): If you want to waive ingress fees, propose either (A) extend to 18 months, or (B) keep 12 months and cap waived amount to $15k. Also we need ARR impact modelling.
Jenny (AE): Customer says they cannot commit to >12 months. They'd accept a short-term credit equal to 2 months of baseline spend instead of extending term. Is that workable?
Lena (DealDesk): A two-month credit is similar to a 16% effective discount if baseline is small. We can entertain that if final effective discount stays <=18%. Anything higher, route to RevOps lead. Also require a clause preventing additional credits for the remainder of the term.
contract-bot: Please attach: current SOW, renewal worksheet, and proposed concession memo. Template: https://redwood.company/contracts/credit-memo-template
Priya (AM): On logs retention - compliance may allow 24m for an add-on fee. Tom, what's the price to bump from 12->24 months?
Tom (Finance): Add-on is $4k/year for their tier. If logs are critical, include that in the PR-REQ as a separately billable item.
Nate (SE): Security artifacts we have: SOC2 report (Q4), penetration test summary, SCIM SSO guide. I can assemble and send to them today. Also recommend: keep baseline at 1 GPU equivalent, burst to 3 for heavy jobs. That keeps price impact low.
Jenny (AE): Sounds good. I'll draft the PR-REQ: include split baseline+consumption model, proposed two-month credit, ingress fee waiver capped at $15k, logs retention add-on optional, and security artifacts packet. Targeting submission today.
Lena (DealDesk): In PR-REQ include churn risk if denied and detailed justification from AE (integration delays + POC metrics). Mark as "hybrid renewal exception". I'll pre-approve routing to RevOps if numbers exceed cap.
Priya (AM): Also confirm customer wants the option to convert consumption to reserved at any time with credit applied pro-rata. That needs a gating clause.
Tom (Finance): If you allow conversions, add a one-time conversion fee of $2k and clear pro-rata math in the contract. Finance will not allow open-ended conversions without limits.
Jenny (AE): Noted. I'll include conversion fee and pro-rata formula: remaining consumption spend credited at baseline rate up to unused committed value.
Lena (DealDesk): Legal will need exact wording but this is acceptable as a negotiation position. Once PR-REQ is in, I'll route and ping RevOps if needed.
Nate (SE): Sending security package to Jenny and Priya now.
Jenny (AE): PR-REQ submitted: https://redwood.company/review/PR-67890 — pinging here for follow-up. Will update when we get approval. :rocket:
Priya (AM): Thanks team. I'll pre-draft the optional 24m logs addendum to speed counterparty sign.
Tom (Finance): I'll benchmark effective discount scenarios and reply in the PR thread.
Lena (DealDesk): Thanks — keep convo in PR thread once submitted so we have audit trail.
Jenny (AE): Will do. Resolving this thread until approvals come back. :white_check_mark:
